ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image is a grid diagram rotated into a diamond direction, composed of several squares. There are white small squares on the periphery, one gray small square on each of the left and right sides, and a larger gray square in the middle. All the small squares look congruent; the side length of the middle gray square is equal to 2 times the side length of a small square. Reasoning: Take the area of one white small square as 1. According to the number of peripheral white small squares in the diagram, there are 10 in total, so the white area is 10. The gray part includes the two gray small squares on the left and right, each with area 1; the side length of the middle gray large square is 2 times that of a small square, and its area is 2×2=4. Therefore the total gray area is 1+4+1=6. The ratio of gray area to white area is 6:10, simplified to 3:5.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, what is the ratio of the area of the gray squares to the area of the white squares?

method.method_draft: First inspect the figure as a tilted grid of congruent small squares. Take one small white perimeter square as 1 unit of area. From the image, count the white unit squares around the border: there are 10. For the gray area, identify the two gray side squares as 1 unit each, and the central gray square as a larger square whose side is twice the small-square side, so its area is 4 unit squares. Thus gray area = 4 + 1 + 1 = 6 units and white area = 10 units; simplify 6:10 to 3:5.
